sentences.text: Cnemiornis is a genus of flightless geese endemic to New Zealand that belongs to the family Anatidae.
These birds were as large as some small moa, with the North Island species weighing 15 kg and the South Island species reaching 18 kg.
The geese were flightless and possessed much-reduced webbing on their feet.
The Māori name for the North Island goose was tarepo.
The genus contains two distinct species: C. gracilis and C. calcitrans.
Richard Owen described the genus Cnemiornis in 1866.
These geese were never particularly common and faced hunting pressures from settling Polynesians.
Their eggs and hatchlings were preyed upon by the Polynesian rat and settlers' dogs.
The fossil range of Cnemiornis extends from the Otiran to the Holocene.
Cnemiornis lived from the Calabrian to the Holocene, between 1.63 and 0 million years ago.
